questions.q: What does g_form represent inside a Client Script?
options: A database table on the server
The form currently rendered on screen, with the values currently sitting in its fields
A collection of every record in the Incident table
The HTTP request that loaded the page
questions.explain: g_form is the browser-side object for the one record the user already has open — not a database query.

options: It permanently saves the record to the database the moment it runs
It runs a GlideRecord query against the sys_user_group table
It does nothing, because getValue() always returns null on load
It sets assignment_group in the browser immediately, without ever querying or writing to the database
questions.explain: setValue() updates what the user sees right away; nothing is written to the database until the record is actually saved.

questions.q: What is the real difference between g_form and GlideRecord?
options: GlideRecord is only usable on the client side
They are two names for the exact same object
GlideRecord reads/writes database rows on the server; g_form reads/writes fields on the form in the browser
g_form can only be used in Business Rules, never in Client Scripts
questions.explain: This is the core distinction the lesson draws: server-side database access vs. client-side form access.

options: justification is deleted from the form permanently
justification becomes not-mandatory and hidden
Nothing changes, because setMandatory and setVisible only run on page load
justification becomes mandatory and visible regardless of the value
questions.explain: needs evaluates to false whenever newValue isn't '1', so both setMandatory(false) and setVisible(false) fire.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call getControl() an 'escape hatch, not a first resort'?
options: Because the named g_form methods keep working across different ServiceNow form renderers in a way raw DOM styling may not
Because getControl() always throws an error in Workspace
Because getControl() can only be called from server-side scripts
Because getControl() is deprecated and no longer works in any version of ServiceNow
questions.explain: getControl() gives you the raw DOM element for edge cases, but the dedicated g_form methods are the more portable first choice.
